key_insight: Nano- and micro-textures in perovskite solar cells do more than trap light—they also improve wetting, crystallinity, charge extraction, and potentially mechanical robustness.
engineering_relevance: Texturing is a multi-functional design strategy that can simultaneously boost efficiency and device reliability in perovskite-based photovoltaics and related optoelectronics.
method: Use nano- or micro-textured interfaces to reduce reflection and enhance light trapping.
Leverage textures to improve perovskite film wetting and crystal growth quality.
Apply texturing to support better carrier extraction and, in flexible devices, lower residual stress under bending.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a review of very recently published texture-related benefits rather than new experimental data, synthesizing evidence across perovskite solar cell studies.
watch_item: The benefits of texturing may depend strongly on texture geometry, processing compatibility, and scalable fabrication control, so not every texture will improve every device property.
paper_title: More than just light management -- The multiple advantages of nano- and micro-textures in perovskite solar cells
